partnershipPlan: Two bereaved relatives from the family advisory group review the question before searching and the board summary before it is sent; one volunteer caller and the social worker comment on which strategies the hospice could deliver.
socialListening: No social media listening; comments from the last year of family feedback cards that mention bereavement follow-up are read for themes.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: At two weeks I was still dealing with the funeral and the bank; if someone had rung a month later I might have said yes.
items.implication: Extract timing carefully and do not assume earlier is better.

items.theme: A group is not for everyone
items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I am not a talking-in-a-circle person, but a cup of tea with one person who knew her would have helped.
items.implication: Separate uptake of group and one-to-one support where studies report both.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Half my calls go to voicemail, and I never know whether to try again or leave them in peace.
items.implication: Extract reach of the first contact and any rules for repeat attempts.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Families in our community would come if the offer came from someone who speaks their language and knows the customs around mourning.
items.implication: Look for studies of interpreter-supported or community-partnered outreach and report their absence if none exist.

summary: Four composite voices on timing, format, reach and language.
